name: Switzerland, canton of Ticino

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary taxation)
paths.note: Dividends are ordinary income at the federal tariff and the Ticino married scale, times the cantonal coefficient (100%) and the communal multiplier (Bellinzona 93%); a portfolio holding under 10% gets no partial taxation; gains on listed shares are tax-free for a private investor (DBG art. 16 para. 3); annual cantonal and communal wealth tax on worldwide net assets; descendants, spouse and ascendants are exempt from inheritance and gift tax (LT art. 154 para. 1 f).

paths.name: Lump-sum taxation (imposizione secondo il dispendio)
paths.note: Income and wealth tax are replaced by the ordinary scales applied to a deemed income of at least the highest of CHF 434,700, 7 times the rent of the home and the living costs, and to a deemed wealth of 5 times that base (LT art. 13, DBG art. 14). No time limit in law while both spouses stay non-Swiss and do not work in Switzerland. Foreign dividends and gains are covered; inheritance follows the ordinary Ticino rules (children exempt).

checks.working: Inputs: a married couple with 3 minor children, no church tax, tax year 2026; taxable income far above every tariff break so the top marginal rates apply; allowances and deductions ignored as in the other recipes. Bellinzona, 2026: cantonal coefficient 100% (LT art. 1b) + communal multiplier 93% (coordinated multiplier 2026, Foglio ufficiale 8 July 2026) = 193%. DIVIDENDS 2,000,000 taxed in full (DBG art. 20 para. 1bis not met; LT art. 19). Federal (DBG art. 36 para. 2, tariff in force since 1 Jan 2026): tax at 941,400 is 108,261.00, plus 11.50 per 100 above = 11.5% of the whole amount; 2,000,000 x 11.5% = 230,000.00 (the CHF 263 per-child reduction of art. 36 para. 2bis, 789 in all, is ignored, as are social deductions and the dividend-free parts). Ticino (LT art. 35 para. 2, married scale; top category rate for 2026 14.0% by art. 309h para. 2): tax at the end of the category ending at 761,400 is 101,102.50 (printed in art. 35 para. 2), plus 14.0% x (2,000,000 - 761,400) = 14.0% x 1,238,600 = 173,404.00, so base tax 274,506.50; x 193% = 529,797.55 (cantonal 274,506.50 + communal 255,291.05). Income tax before credit 230,000.00 + 529,797.55 = 759,797.55. Flat-rate credit for the 15% treaty withholding on foreign dividends (SR 672.201): 15% x 2,000,000 = 300,000.00, below the Swiss tax on those dividends. Dividend tax after credit 459,797.55. GAINS 1,000,000: nil (DBG art. 16 para. 3; LT art. 15 para. 3). WEALTH 100,000,000: deductions 60,000 for the couple + 3 x 30,000 for the minor children (art. 48) = 150,000, taxable 99,850,000; scale of art. 49 para. 1: tax at the end of the 700,001-1,380,000 band is 3,450.00, then 2.5 per mille above: 2.5 per mille x (99,850,000 - 1,380,000) = 246,175.00, base tax 249,625.00; x 193% = 481,776.25. Burden cap (art. 49a): cantonal and communal tax 529,797.55 + 481,776.25 = 1,011,573.80 is below 60% x 2,000,000 = 1,200,000 (and the 1% minimum yield, 1,000,000, is below the dividends), so no relief. Total 459,797.55 + 481,776.25 = 941,573.80.
checks.model_note: The engine applies one flat marginal rate of 38.52% (11.5% federal + 14% x 193%) to every franc of dividends, whereas the Ticino scale is progressive below CHF 761,400: the law's cantonal and communal tax on CHF 2M is 529,797.55 instead of 2,000,000 x 27.02% = 540,400, i.e. 10,602.45 lower.

checks.working: The tax does not depend on the actual dividends, gains or wealth (foreign income and assets are covered), only on the deemed base, which this check ASSUMES to be a round CHF 1,000,000 (7 times a rent of about CHF 12,000 a month; LT art. 13 para. 3 b, DBG art. 14 para. 3 b); the real base depends on rent and living costs, see open questions. Married couple with 3 children, no church tax, tax year 2026, Bellinzona (193%). Federal (DBG art. 14 para. 4: ordinary tariff art. 36 para. 2, but without the per-child reduction of art. 36 para. 2bis, second sentence): 108,261.00 + 11.50 x 586 (the 58,600 above 941,400, in hundreds) = 115,000.00. Income tax on the base (LT art. 13 para. 4, art. 35 para. 2, 14.0% top category rate for 2026): 101,102.50 + 14.0% x (1,000,000 - 761,400) = 101,102.50 + 33,404.00 = 134,506.50; x 193% = 259,597.55 (134,506.50 x 1.93 = 259,597.545). Deemed wealth tax: the taxable wealth is 5 times the base (art. 13 para. 5) = 5,000,000, with no deductions: 3,450.00 + 2.5 per mille x (5,000,000 - 1,380,000) = 3,450.00 + 9,050.00 = 12,500.00; x 193% = 24,125.00. Total 115,000.00 + 259,597.55 + 24,125.00 = 398,722.55.

The family's real case with more wealth so that the cap binds: CHF 600,000 of dividends, CHF 50M of wealth. Bellinzona 2026 (coefficient 100% + 93%), couple with 3 children, no church tax. Federal (DBG art. 36 para. 2): 5,692.00 at 152,400 plus 13.00 per 100 above, so 5,692.00 + 0.13 x (600,000 - 152,400) = 63,880.00 (per-child reduction of CHF 789 ignored). Cantonal and communal income tax (LT art. 35 para. 2): tax at 303,900 is 34,080.35 (printed), plus 14.65% x (600,000 - 303,900) = 43,378.65, so 77,459.00; x 193% = 149,495.87. WEALTH: taxable 50,000,000 - 150,000 = 49,850,000; base tax 3,450.00 + 2.5 per mille x 48,470,000 = 124,625.00; x 193% = 240,526.25 before the cap. Burden cap (LT art. 49a): 149,495.87 + 240,526.25 = 390,022.12 exceeds 60% x 600,000 = 360,000 (the 1% minimum yield, 500,000, is below the dividends), so the wealth tax is cut to 360,000 - 149,495.87 = 210,504.13. Federal 63,880.00 + cantonal and communal 360,000.00 = 423,880.00, less the credit of 15% x 600,000 = 90,000.00. Total 333,880.00.
checks.model_note: The engine applies a flat 11.5% federal rate to dividends, whereas the federal tariff at CHF 600,000 gives 63,880 (10.65%): the cap equalises the cantonal parts, so the engine total is 339,000 = 360,000 - 21,000 and the law's is 333,880; difference 5,120.00 = 69,000 - 63,880.

checks.working: Descendants are exempt from inheritance and gift tax in Ticino whatever the amount: LT art. 154 para. 1 f ('il coniuge, il partner registrato, gli ascendenti e discendenti in linea diretta, compresi gli adottivi'). Art. 155 para. 2 (the first CHF 10,000 a year) is not needed. There is no federal inheritance tax. Estate 10,000,000 to 3 children: tax 0.

assumptions: The family is two non-Swiss spouses who have not been Swiss tax residents for 10 years and do not work in Switzerland, so lump-sum taxation is open to them (LT art. 13 para. 1-2; DBG art. 14). Both must qualify.

Bellinzona, tax year 2026: cantonal coefficient 100% and communal multiplier 93%, no church tax. Lugano, where most families settle, has a lower multiplier (about 80%; the coordinated 2026 multiplier is 81%): its top rate would be about 36.8% and the wealth tax about 0.45%; the council's final decision on the 2026 multiplier was not confirmed, so the tax file keeps Bellinzona.

The top category rate of the married scale is the 2026 value, 14.0% (art. 309h para. 2); it falls to 13.5% in 2027, 13.0% in 2028, 12.5% in 2029 and a 12% maximum effective rate from 2030. The projection uses 2026 rates throughout.

The lump-sum base is shown at CHF 1,000,000, the representative used for every canton. The family's actual base is the highest of CHF 434,700 (federal minimum CHF 435,000), 7 times the rent or rental value of the home and the living costs; with the prime-rent sample of CHF 4,300 a month (CHF 361,200) the minimum would bind and the lump sum would be about CHF 150,000.

A Swiss family foundation (ZGB art. 335) is not offered as a path: it is taxed as a legal entity, its distributions are taxable for the beneficiaries, and in Ticino, where descendants inherit free of tax, it brings no advantage over holding personally.
Treaty relief on foreign dividends is assumed to be claimed only if the control calculation stays below the lump sum; the 15% withholding is then a final cost.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the lump sum is a fixed amount per regime, but by law it is the tax on a base of at least the highest of CHF 434,700, 7 times the rent and the family's worldwide living costs (LT art. 13 para. 3; DBG art. 14 para. 3), with deemed wealth 5 times the base (para. 5). The engine would need the base as a function of the family's spending and housing cost.

Needs an engine change: modified lump sum. Claiming treaty-reduced withholding on foreign dividends puts that income into the control calculation at the ordinary scales (LT art. 13 para. 6 f, DBG art. 14 para. 3 d); the tax is the higher of the two. The engine charges 15% on every foreign dividend and ignores it.
Needs an engine change: the Ticino income scale is progressive; the engine applies the top marginal rate to every franc of dividends (about CHF 10,600 too high on a CHF 2M income).
Needs an engine change: scheduled rate changes: the top category rate falls to 13.5% (2027), 13.0% (2028), 12.5% (2029) and a 12% effective maximum from 2030 (LT art. 309g-309h).
The tax-free CHF 200,000 and the CHF 60,000 / 30,000 wealth deductions are not indexed (art. 39 LT indexes income-tax scale and deductions only); the lump-sum minimum is (art. 13 para. 8).
2026 top rate: LT art. 309h para. 2 sets 14% for the top category; whether it also caps the 14.65% bracket (CHF 304,000-761,400) is unclear; if so, tax is about CHF 4-6k lower a year.
Bellinzona's own 2026 multiplier for individuals: 93 is the coordinated figure (ti.ch FU-MCC2026).
